question: Assume today is 2026-08-23. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of live births in South Korea in July 2026, as it will be first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Population Trends release.

target.what: Number of live births occurring in South Korea during July 2026, as first published in Statistics Korea's monthly Population Trends (인구동향) release
target.publisher: Statistics Korea (KOSTAT), monthly Population Trends / 인구동향
target.cadence: monthly, with a lag of roughly 2-3 months after month-end (July data typically first published around late September/October)
target.caveats: Target is births by month of occurrence (occurrence-based), not by registration date; KOSTAT monthly provisional figures are occurrence-based and later revised. Working interpretation: all live births to residents of South Korea regardless of place of birth (domestic occurrence basis as used by KOST

candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 births follow the recent level and seasonal pattern of monthly births; July is typically a relatively high-birth month in Korea. Recent monthly values (2024-2026) plus year-over-year change give a baseline nowcast.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly live birth counts for South Korea from KOSTAT Population Trends for Jan 2023 through the latest month published before 2026-08-23 (likely May or June 2026), plus the same months in 2024 and 2025 to compute YoY growth and July seasonal factor.
search_hints: Statistics Korea monthly live births 2026 인구동향

candidates.hypothesis: Korean births are strongly linked to marriages roughly 1-2 years earlier; marriage registrations rose in 2023-2024, which should support 2025-2026 births. Monthly marriage counts lead births and can adjust the own-history baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly marriage registration counts for South Korea 2022-2026 (through latest available before cutoff), and the historical lag correlation between marriages and births (roughly 10-24 months).

candidates.perspective: Births by birth order / maternal age
candidates.hypothesis: Total births decompose into first births and higher-order births; first-birth trends track marriage cohorts while higher-order births track prior births. This constrains the level and direction of change.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly or quarterly births by birth order and by mother's age for 2024-2026, and the share of first births in total births.
search_hints: Korea births by birth order 2025 statistics

candidates.hypothesis: Resident registration (주민등록) birth registrations and 'birth support' applications provide a near-real-time administrative trace that correlates with occurrence-based births with a short lag.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly resident-registration births or birth-related administrative counts (e.g., 첫만남이용권 applications, 아동수당 신청) for mid-2026, and the historical ratio to KOSTAT occurrence births.

candidates.hypothesis: KOSTAT and research institutes publish annual birth projections and sometimes monthly commentary; these constrain the plausible 2026 level and July share.
candidates.data_to_find: Any 2026 annual birth forecast or monthly nowcast published before 2026-08-23, and KOSTAT's 2026 population projections for births.

candidates.hypothesis: July births reflect conceptions around October of the prior year; the July share of annual births is stable and can convert an annual estimate into a July figure. Calendar (lunar, holidays) effects are modest.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical July share of annual births for 2015-2025, and any documented seasonal pattern in Korean monthly births.
search_hints: Korea monthly births seasonality July share

candidates.hypothesis: Pronatalist policies (2024-2026), immigration, and COVID-era conception dips affect the level; identifying measurable policy effects or cohort sizes helps adjust the baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: Evidence of policy-driven changes in births in 2025-2026, and the size of the 2021-2022 conception dip that would affect 2026 births.
search_hints: South Korea birth policy effect 2025 2026 births

Own-history route: July 2025 (21,803), May 2026 (23,160) and Jan–May 2026 cumulative (122,694) give the recent level and trend; series_auto multiplies last July's value by the YoY growth of the latest months. Shared dependency: all three points are KOSTAT monthly releases; failure mode is a short series with only one July observation.

previous_assumptions.name: July 2026 YoY growth factor applied to July 2025 births
previous_assumptions.rationale: 2026 monthly YoY growth has run +13.6% (Feb), +13.6% (May), +15.2% cumulative Jan–May; July 2025 was itself +5.9% YoY, so a slightly lower 2026 growth than the spring peak is plausible as the marriage-registration decline (Feb −4.2%, May −6.4%) starts to bite. Central 1.12 with a wide band spanning near-flat to continued double-digit growth.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: July 2026 continues the 2026 upswing at a somewhat moderated pace relative to spring 2026.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: June 2026 births (published late August) showing YoY growth below ~5% or above ~20%.

previous_assumptions.name: July share of 2026 annual live births
previous_assumptions.rationale: Long-run July share is 7.8% (p173); 2025 monthly shares show July between the June trough (7.9%) and the autumn peak, and daily-average deviations put July above the annual average. 8.3% is a modest upward adjustment for the recent shift toward higher summer shares, with a band spanning the long-run 7.8% to 9.0%.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 seasonal pattern resembles the recent (2020s) pattern rather than the 1981–2023 average.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: KOSTAT monthly shares for 2026 showing July below 7.5% or above 9.5%.

previous_assumptions.rationale: Jan–May 2026 cumulative 122,694 (+15.2%) and Jan–Jun ~146,162 imply a full-year total well above 2025's 254,457; the Seoul Shinmun 'late 200,000s' projection and the sustained double-digit growth support ~285,000, with a band from 265,000 to 305,000.

methods.rationale: YoY-scaling route: July 2025 births (21,803) times a July 2026 growth factor anchored on the 2026 monthly YoY growth (+13.6% May, +15.2% cumulative Jan-May), moderated for the marriage-registration decline. Shared dependency: p16 and a1 both derive from KOSTAT monthly releases; failure mode is a sharp break in the 2026 upswing.

methods.label: m2

a3.role: 2026 annual live births in South Korea

methods.rationale: Annual-level times seasonal-share route: 2026 annual births (~285,000, anchored on Jan–May 2026 cumulative 122,694 and the sustained upswing) times the July share (~8.3%, anchored on the long-run 7.8% and recent monthly shares). The earlier p4 anchor was removed because it made the unit birth*year/(month*month); the formula now yields live births/month directly. Shared dependency: a3 and a2 both r

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
